title: Anatomy of an ad: judge the five parts, not the whole
hook: “This ad worked” tells you nothing you can brief. Which part of it worked?
caption:
“This ad worked” tells you nothing you can brief. Which part of it worked?

Every ad has five parts: hook, cast, pacing, CTA and setting. Judge the whole ad and a win only teaches you to remake it. Judge the parts and a win tells you what to carry forward.

This is the idea behind Decode, which tags 50+ attributes on every ad. We price the attribute, not the ad.

You can try a manual version today with a sheet and your last ten ads. The steps are on the last slide. Save it.

slides.headline: Every ad has *five parts*. Judge each one separately.
slides.sub: How we take an ad apart before we call it a winner.

slides.headline: “It worked” *cannot be briefed*
slides.body:
When the whole ad is the unit, a win teaches you to make the same ad again.

When the parts are the unit, a win tells you what to carry into the next ten.

slides.headline: *Hook* and *cast*
items: Hook: what the first seconds show and say
Cast: who is on screen, and who they resemble

slides.headline: *Pacing*, CTA and *setting*
items: Pacing: how fast it cuts, when the product appears
CTA: what it asks for, and when
Setting: where it happens (home, studio, street)

slides.headline: attributes tagged by Decode on *every ad*, inside these five parts
Try it on your *last ten ads*
items: One row per ad, one column per part
Fill each cell in three words
Add cost per order in the last column
Sort by cost and read down each column

slides.headline: Stop grading ads. *Grade the parts.*
slides.sub: Save this and try it on ten ads today.
actions: Send to whoever reviews your ads

notes:
Reader: a performance marketer who reviews creative weekly. One argument: the unit of learning is the part of the ad, so tag hook, cast, pacing, CTA and setting separately. Shape: breakdown plus a same-day exercise. Numbers used: 50+ attributes per ad (facts bank, Decode). The five parts are the ones named in the spec. Topic kept.
